executive_actions.a_rejected_order_is_ap: A rejected order is appended to the same register it would have joined — the rejection itself is the public record (Art. II §2).
executive_actions.active_emergency_power: Active emergency powers — these widen the delegated scope only within their declared area and duration · Art. II §7 · CLK-03:
executive_actions.electoral_judicial_and: electoral, judicial, and legislative process domains are rejected unconditionally — the engine validates the order pre-issuance · Art. III §2 · Art. II §7
executive_actions.executive_orders_execu: Executive orders execute the delegated scope; they are validated before issuance and remain judicially reviewable at any time (Art. IV §5). The order lifecycle:
executive_actions.full_and_equal_investi: Full and equal investigative power over overseen departments · Art. III §4 — findings publish to the public record; the outcome branch files a proposal, a removal request, or a legislative referral, or closes with no finding.
executive_actions.leave_blank_for_an_exe: Leave blank for an executive-wide investigation.
executive_actions.no_applications_submit: No applications submitted against these lines.
executive_actions.no_delegated_scope_exi: No delegated scope exists yet — F-LEG-014.
executive_actions.no_delegated_scope_yet: no delegated scope yet — the delegation act has not enacted (F-LEG-014)
executive_actions.no_orders_issued_the_s: No orders issued — the scope-validation rails apply from the first order.
executive_actions.order_register_issued_: Order register — issued and rejected on one record
executive_actions.orders_policy_proposal: Orders, policy proposals, investigations, and grants — all within the authority the legislature delegated. The engine validates scope before anything takes effect: an order outside the delegated scope is rejected before issuance, and the rejection itself goes on the public record. Every issued order remains judicially reviewable.
executive_actions.scope_validation_happe: Scope validation happens before issuance — an order outside the delegated scope is rejected and never takes effect. Elections, sessions, and courts cannot be disrupted, even under emergency powers.
executive_actions.the_executive_proposes: The executive proposes; the department board adopts, amends, or declines — proposals do not bypass the board · Art. III §4.
executive_actions.the_legislature_approp: The legislature appropriates by act; the executive administers. Awards never exceed the line's remaining balance, and every award and disbursement is appended to the audit chain · WF-SYS-04.
executive_actions.the_legislature_has_ap: The legislature has appropriated no funds — appropriation is an act. Open a bill →
executive_actions.the_live_instrument_th: The live instrument the order executes — a delegation/charter act or an active emergency power. The order may not exceed it.
executive_actions.the_order_may_name_a_d: The order may name a department this executive oversees.
executive_actions.the_order_never_took_e: {constitutionError} The order never took effect; the rejected attempt is on the public record — see the top of the register below.
executive_actions.this_executive_is_stil: This executive is still {status}. Orders issue from a delegated or elected executive only.
executive_departmentdetail.a_chartered_d: A chartered department, its Board of Governors, and the consent pipeline that seats it. The governors hold 10-year civil terms (CLK-09); the worker-elected seats run on the legislative-term clock (CLK-10) — the two clocks sit side by side in the roster below.
executive_departmentdetail.a_good_faith_: A good-faith competence/ethics finding — published at filing.
executive_departmentdetail.cgc_intellect: CGC intellectual property is perpetually public domain · Art. III §5
executive_departmentdetail.consent_faile: Consent failed — the seat reopens for renomination (WF-EXE-05).
executive_departmentdetail.consent_vote_: Consent vote · F-LEG-020 · majority of all serving
executive_departmentdetail.credentials_a: Credentials and the neutrality attestation — published at nomination.
executive_departmentdetail.full_and_equa: full and equal investigative power · Art. III §4 · executive actions →
executive_departmentdetail.governor_remo: Governor removal is an ordinary majority of all serving — hiring and firing (owner ruling #14). This is deliberately not the supermajority machinery used to remove elected officeholders.
executive_departmentdetail.governors_10_: Governors: 10-year civil appointments · CLK-09. Worker-elected seats end with the legislative term · CLK-10. Chair: joint-elected by the entire board · Art. III §6.
executive_departmentdetail.last_filed_re: Last filed: {kind} report on {fmtDate}. on the public record →
executive_departmentdetail.no_common_goo: No Common Good Corporations overseen by this department.
executive_departmentdetail.no_nomination: No nominations on record. A seated member of the overseeing executive opens one below.
executive_departmentdetail.opens_an_ordi: opens an ordinary-majority chamber vote (NOT supermajority) · owner ruling #14 · Art. III §4.
executive_departmentdetail.opens_the_f_l: opens the F-LEG-020 consent vote in the legislature · majority of all serving · Art. III §4.
executive_departmentdetail.removal_runs_: Removal runs against a currently seated board member.
executive_departmentdetail.removal_vote_: Removal vote · majority of all serving
executive_departmentdetail.the_board_and: The board and its governor seats are created when the department is chartered (F-LEG-016); governors are nominated (F-EXE-001) and consented (F-LEG-020) onto them.
executive_departmentdetail.the_nominee_s: The nominee's user id. Eligibility is active jurisdiction association only — neutrality is a duty of office, not an eligibility test (Art. I).
executive_departmentdetail.there_is_no_c: There is no currently seated board member to file a removal against.
executive_departmentdetail.this_charter_: This charter sets no reporting interval — reporting cadence is charter data, not a clock.
executive_departmentdetail.two_clocks_cl: two clocks · CLK-09 governors · CLK-10 worker seats
executive_departmentreporting.a_short_la: A short label for this special report.
executive_departmentreporting.both_regis: Both registers below read publicly. Filed by this department's seated governors (R-18) — the engine is the boundary, so the filing forms appear only for them.
executive_departmentreporting.catalog_al: catalog alias: F-GOV-001 · drafts publish for comment · emergency-enabled rules expire with the power (CLK-03).
catalog alias: F-GOV-002 · recipients fixed: Executive + legislature · published · WF-SYS-03.
executive_departmentreporting.charter_la: Charter law, an in-force enabling act, or an ACTIVE emergency power — the engine rejects scope overruns with the citation.
executive_departmentreporting.expires_wi: {label} expires with the emergency power · CLK-03
executive_departmentreporting.registers_: Registers are public; filing is the board's.
executive_departmentreporting.reporting_: reporting interval (months) — charter data, not a clock
executive_departmentreporting.reports_fi: Reports file to the executive AND the legislature, published to the public record. Filing a periodic report seeds the next obligation; a missed due date is swept to overdue (WF-EXE-09).
executive_departmentreporting.rules_and_: Rules and reports are the Board of Governors' implementation layer (Art. III §4): rules carry the act that enables them and can never exceed it; reports keep the executive and the legislature informed and become public record. An emergency- enabled rule is bound to the life of its power — when CLK-03 expires the power, the rule expires with it.
executive_departmentreporting.rules_impl: rules implement, they cannot exceed · Art. III §4
Rules implement — they cannot exceed — the charter and the enabling acts. An emergency-enabled rule expires with its power; nothing rolls over silently.
Rules implement — they cannot exceed — the charter and enabling acts.
executive_departmentreporting.the_first_: The first periodic obligation seeds when the department begins operating and its charter sets a reporting interval.
executive_departmentreporting.there_is_n: There is no charter, in-force act, or active emergency power to cite yet — a rule cannot issue without a live instrument behind it (Art. III §2).
executive_departmentreporting.this_is_wh: This is where a department's board does its day-to-day work: writing the rules that put laws into practice, and filing regular operational and financial reports to both the executive and the legislature. Everything filed here is public record.
executive_departmentreporting.when_a_gov: When a governor files the first rule, it appears here with the act that enables it. The implement-don't-exceed rule binds from the first rule.
executive_departments.a_department_is_cr: A department is created by an ordinary-majority legislative act (F-LEG-016). The constitution names five — {CONSTITUTIONAL_KINDS} — and others may be created by act.
executive_departments.an_open_governor_r: An open governor-removal request splices a live removal_requested state into the machine without disturbing the stored status · Art. III §4.
executive_departments.department_creatio: Department creation is a legislative act at ordinary majority — it names the department, its kind (Chief Executive, Treasury, Defense, State, Justice, or other), the overseeing executive, the charter, and the reporting interval. Institution-creating forms ride the bill flow; there is no side-door POST.
executive_departments.departments_are_cr: Departments are created by legislative act, chartered for a specific function, and run by an appointed Board of Governors under executive oversight. Workers get board seats here exactly as they do in private organizations (co-determination): the first worker-elected seat arrives at 100 workers.
executive_departments.governor_removal_i: Governor removal is an ordinary majority of all serving — hiring and firing. Supermajority applies only where the constitution states it; it does not apply here.
executive_departments.no_civil_officers_: No civil officers seated — duties run through the chartered departments per their charters · Art. II §9 · CLK-09.
executive_departments.no_nominations_in_: No nominations in flight — open one from a department's detail page (F-EXE-001).
executive_departments.nomination_dossier: Nomination dossier · F-EXE-001 → Consent vote · F-LEG-020 → Seated · R-18 — live appointments across all departments.
executive_departments.owner_ruling_14_ar: owner ruling #14 · Art. III §4 · file from the department detail page (F-EXE-003)
executive_home.a_delegated_committee_car: A delegated committee carries no term of its own: each member's term IS their legislative seat's term (ESM-16). The office never outlives the chamber that delegated it.
executive_home.an_elected_executive_runs: An elected executive runs in lockstep with the legislative election — the two elections share one clock, and neither can be skipped or delayed.
executive_home.conversion_adopted_on_the: Conversion adopted on the chamber supermajority alone
executive_home.conversion_needs_the_cham: Conversion needs the chamber's own supermajority — ceil(serving × 2/3) — AND a supermajority of the constituent jurisdictions, each counted independently. Both meters resolve through the protected functions; nothing on this page is computed client-side.
executive_home.conversion_to_elected_off: Conversion to elected office — dual supermajority
executive_home.creation_act_delegation_b: Creation act — delegation by the legislature
executive_home.delegated_by_default_conv: delegated by default · converts only by dual supermajority · Art. III §2–3
executive_home.dual_supermajority_acts_r: Dual-supermajority acts ride the bill flow; the legislature votes and the engine opens the constituent leg. This page renders the process, it never originates a vote.
executive_home.elected_committee_pr_stv_: Elected committee · PR-STV winners with equal decision-making power · Art. III §2.
executive_home.forming_the_stub_awaits_t: Forming — the stub awaits the delegation act.
executive_home.introduce_a_conversion_bi: Introduce a conversion bill → filed by a member of the source legislature (R-09)
executive_home.introduce_a_delegation_bi: Introduce a delegation bill → filed by a member of the source legislature (R-09)
executive_home.no_conversion_on_record_c: No conversion on record. Converting a delegated executive into a directly elected office is a dual-supermajority act — the chamber's own supermajority AND a supermajority of the constituent jurisdictions, each counted independently (Art. III §3 · Art. VII).
executive_home.no_delegation_act_on_reco: No delegation act on record. The legislature delegates executive authority by supermajority act — members remain seated legislators (Art. III §2).
executive_home.no_departments_chartered_: No departments chartered yet. Departments are created by the legislature by ordinary act (F-LEG-016 · Art. II §9); oversight is assigned to this executive in the act. Open the department registry →
executive_home.no_direct_constituent_jur: No direct constituent jurisdiction holds a legislature able to vote, so the conversion completes on the chamber's own supermajority (Art. III §3). The executive election schedules from here.
executive_home.no_office_term_delegated_: no office term — delegated members run on their legislative seats
executive_home.one_clock_drives_both_ele: one clock drives both elections · Art. III §3 · CLK-10
executive_home.selected_proportionally_t: Selected proportionally — the same method as legislative committees · Art. III §2 · ledger #q2. Delegated members are ex-officio legislators: each remains a seated member of the chamber, and the office's authority is the chamber's.
executive_home.steps_in_in_rank_order_if: Steps in, in rank order, if the office vacates — the popular count, not an appointment, decides succession (sequential exclusion · Art. III §3).
executive_home.term_one_clock_drives_bot: Term — one clock drives both elections
executive_home.term_sync_on_the_chamber_: term sync on the chamber page →
executive_home.the_executive_is_delegate: The executive is delegated by default and exists as a stub from the moment a jurisdiction is set up. Conversion to a directly elected office is the only path to an independent executive, and it is deliberately hard: a supermajority of the chamber AND a supermajority of the constituent jurisdictions must each agree. The model card above always shows the office's real footing — never a demo toggle.
executive_home.the_executive_is_the_gove: The executive is the government's doing arm — it carries out the laws, runs the departments, and answers to the legislature that created it. Every executive starts as a committee delegated by the legislature. A supermajority — plus a supermajority of the places that make it up, where they exist — can convert it to a directly elected office, as either a committee of five or more equal officers, or a single individual with four advisors. Executive terms always equal the legislative term.
executive_home.the_office_is_in_a_transi: The office is in a transitional state — see the conversion record below for where it stands in the dual-supermajority process.
executive_home.the_supermajority_that_de: The supermajority that delegated the office
executive_home.this_executive_was_create: This executive was created as a stub at jurisdiction setup. It holds no members until the legislature delegates authority to it by supermajority act ( · WF-EXE-01). Until then, the office exists only as a constitutional placeholder.
